name: Schloss Rotholz Buch in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: Schloss Rotholz in Buch in Tirol: stately 1575 Renaissance hunting lodge built by Archduke Ferdinand II, today the cradle of Tyrolean alpine cheese making.
beschreibung:
Overview

Steeped in history, Schloss Rotholz is picturesquely situated on a gentle terrace at the foot of the Rofan Mountains in the municipality of Buch in Tirol (Schwaz district) at an elevation of around 540 meters. Strategically positioned where the Zillertal meets the Tyrolean Inntal near the market town of Jenbach, this stately Renaissance castle represents an outstanding architectural monument of Habsburg regional history. With its impressive four-wing complex, distinctive oriel towers, and manicured castle grounds, the estate blends princely hunting heritage with more than 150 years of history as the birthplace of Tyrolean agricultural and dairy education.

History & Agricultural Cradle

The estate's roots trace back to the 16th century: between 1575 and 1585, the art-loving Tyrolean sovereign Erzherzog Ferdinand II. commissioned court architect Alberto Lucchese to transform the older residence Ansitz Rotholz into a magnificent hunting lodge. Ferdinand utilized the castle as a summer residence and base for extended hunts across the game-rich forests of the Inntal and Zillertal. In 1705, ownership passed to the influential Counts of Tannenberg (Grafen von Tannenberg), who modernized the building in Baroque style and established the noteworthy Baroque castle chapel dedicated to the Holy Family. In 1879, the Tyrolean provincial parliament (Tiroler Landtag) purchased the castle estate, founding the esteemed Landwirtschaftliche Landeslehranstalt Rotholz and Austria's first dairy school. To this day, Rotholz remains the intellectual and practical hub of Tyrolean mountain farming, Zillertal hay-milk processing, and traditional artisan cheese production. The historic castle chapel, boasting a splendid Baroque altar and intricate stucco work, has been faithfully preserved in its original condition.

Visit & Getting There

The exterior of Schloss Rotholz, the historic courtyard facades, and the castle park can be viewed from the outside year-round free of charge. Because the castle building serves as an active educational center and administrative headquarters of the Higher Federal College and Research Institute for Agriculture and Nutrition, the interior rooms are generally not open to the public (the castle chapel opens for religious services and guided tours). Located directly adjacent to the castle is the modern visitor center and farm shop of the Rotholzer Genusswelt, where visitors can taste award-winning Rotholz cheese specialties. Getting there by car: take the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Wiesing/Zillertal or Jenbach), continuing on the B171 to Buch in Tirol/Rotholz; free parking is available directly on the castle grounds (Rotholz 46). By public transport: take the ÖBB train to Jenbach station, from where bus route 4011 or 4014 brings you directly to the Rotholz Schule stop (just a two-minute walk).

Tips

The castle park and paved pathways surrounding the castle are completely flat and barrier-free, making them ideal for strolls with wheelchairs or strollers. Be sure to stop by the affiliated farm shop, Rotholzer Hofladen: here you can purchase traditionally aged Rotholz mountain cheese, hay-milk Camembert, and fine Tyrolean schnapps produced directly on site by the school's own dairy and distillery.
